stem: What is the primary anatomical definition of conjunctivitis?

options.text: Inflammation of the mucous membrane lining the outer part of the eye and the inner eyelids
Infection of the corneal epithelium causing localised redness and blurred vision
Inflammation of the lacrimal gland and tear drainage system
Swelling of the sclera caused by an autoimmune response
Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body

explanation: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the conjunctiva, the mucous membrane that lines the inner eyelids and covers the exposed surface of the eye.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the conjunctiva is the mucous membrane lining the inner eyelids and the exposed outer surface of the eye.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this describes keratitis, which involves the cornea rather than the conjunctiva.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this describes lacrimal system inflammation, such as dacryoadenitis or dacryocystitis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because inflammation of the sclera is scleritis, not conjunctivitis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this describes uveitis, which affects the iris and ciliary body.

source.hint: Consider which specific membrane lines the upper and lower fornices.
